desc:
The equalizing cost of a group of numbers is the smallest total number of unit steps (raise or lower one number by 1) needed to make all of them equal; equivalently, the minimum over integers c of the sum of |x - c|.

Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray of nums whose equalizing cost is at most budget.

nums = [1, 4, 2, 9, 3], budget = 8
[4,2,9,3] -> make all 3: 1 + 1 + 6 + 0 = 8   (fits)
the whole array costs 10 (make all 3)          (too much)
answer = 4
hints: A single element always costs 0, so the answer is at least 1. Adding an element to a subarray never makes its cost smaller. What does that suggest?
Because of that monotonicity, two pointers work: grow the right end, and while the window is too expensive, advance the left end.

You need the equalizing cost of the current window quickly after each add and remove: keep the window in two heaps (lower and upper half) with the sum of each half, and delete the leaving element lazily.
editorial: Cost is monotone under inclusion: if window A is contained in window B, then cost(A) ≤ cost(B), because the best common target for B also works for A and B only has extra non-negative terms. So if a window is affordable, all its sub-windows are, which is exactly the condition for the standard two-pointer technique: for each right end, the smallest valid left end never moves left.

Maintain the window in a two-heap median structure with half sums: lower half in a max-heap, upper half in a min-heap, cost sum(hi) - sum(lo) + (|lo| - |hi|) * median. When the right end advances, insert the new element; while the cost exceeds the budget, remove nums[left] (lazy deletion by index) and advance left. Track the largest window length seen.

Each element is inserted once and removed at most once, each in O(log n) amortised, so the whole scan is O(n log n) time with O(n) space. A binary search on the length combined with the sliding cost computation would also work but adds a log factor and is not needed.
solution:
import heapq


class TwoHeaps:
    """lo = max-heap of the lower half (size = size of hi, or one more), hi = min-heap of the upper half."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.lo, self.hi = [], []          # entries (-value, id) and (value, id)
        self.dead = set()                  # ids removed but still sitting inside a heap
        self.side = {}                     # id -> 0 (in lo) or 1 (in hi)
        self.nlo = self.nhi = 0            # live sizes
        self.slo = self.shi = 0            # live sums

    def _clean(self, h):
        while h and h[0][1] in self.dead:
            self.dead.discard(heapq.heappop(h)[1])

    def add(self, i, x):
        self._clean(self.lo)
        if self.nlo == 0 or x <= -self.lo[0][0]:
            heapq.heappush(self.lo, (-x, i))
            self.side[i] = 0
            self.nlo += 1
            self.slo += x
        else:
            heapq.heappush(self.hi, (x, i))
            self.side[i] = 1
            self.nhi += 1
            self.shi += x
        self._balance()

    def remove(self, i, x):
        if self.side.pop(i) == 0:
            self.nlo -= 1
            self.slo -= x
        else:
            self.nhi -= 1
            self.shi -= x
        self.dead.add(i)
        self._balance()

    def _balance(self):
        while self.nlo > self.nhi + 1:
            self._clean(self.lo)
            nx, i = heapq.heappop(self.lo)
            heapq.heappush(self.hi, (-nx, i))
            self.side[i] = 1
            self.nlo -= 1
            self.nhi += 1
            self.slo += nx
            self.shi -= nx
        while self.nhi > self.nlo:
            self._clean(self.hi)
            x, i = heapq.heappop(self.hi)
            heapq.heappush(self.lo, (-x, i))
            self.side[i] = 0
            self.nhi -= 1
            self.nlo += 1
            self.shi -= x
            self.slo += x

    def median2(self):
        """Twice the median of the live values."""
        self._clean(self.lo)
        if self.nlo > self.nhi:
            return -2 * self.lo[0][0]
        self._clean(self.hi)
        return -self.lo[0][0] + self.hi[0][0]

    def cost(self):
        """Minimum total |x - c| over the live values."""
        self._clean(self.lo)
        med = -self.lo[0][0]
        return self.shi - self.slo + (self.nlo - self.nhi) * med


def longestEqualizable(nums, budget):
    t = TwoHeaps()
    left = 0
    best = 0
    for right, x in enumerate(nums):
        t.add(right, x)
        while t.cost() > budget:
            t.remove(left, nums[left])
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best
